handback.feature: Code alone decides from each agent's JSON hand-back (plan.json, work.json, review.json) whether it can be posted, and a rejection says exactly why on the issue.
handback.split_rule: R1 and R2: the ask now needs about 19 criteria, and it holds independent goals (the planner's plan.json; the worker's and reviewer's files; the reviewer's list of the owner's asks). Each story lands on its own and main works after each.
promises: P1 plan.json is one of the allowed kinds (story, feature, question) with every required field -> story 1 (kinds) and story 3 (feature and question fields)
P2 every acceptance criterion's source points at this issue or one of its comments -> story 1
P3 every non-functional requirement has a reason -> already built (dokima/planner.py, from_kind); kept by its current tests
P4 every criterion is proven by a test the plan names; every named test exists and names a criterion of this plan -> story 1
P5 every new test has a docstring whose first line is one plain sentence -> story 2
P6 every new test fails on today's code -> story 2
P7 every changed, renamed or deleted older test has a reason; a rename is a change, not a new test -> story 2
P8 only files under tests/ change -> already built (dokima/planner.py, problems); kept by its current tests
P9 a feature has 2 to 5 stories (already built) whose depends_on point at its own stories with no loops -> story 3
P10 a question ends in '?' (already built) and has a recommended option -> story 3
P11 a rejection says exactly why on the issue -> story 1 and 2 (planner, already posted by planner.yml), story 4 (worker and reviewer)
P12 work.json and review.json have every required field in their prompts' shape, or the run is rejected and the issue says why -> story 4
P13 the reviewer blocks only on a promise with no proof or a proof that proves nothing, and every block names its criterion -> story 4
P14 real JSON hand-backs from this run are kept as test samples once the format is settled (owner's answer 1) -> story 5
P15 every blocker names a criterion (owner's answer 3) -> story 4

P16 the reviewer reads the owner's issue text on its own and lists every ask, each matched to a criterion or marked missing, in a review.json field; the checker rejects a plan review without it (owner's answer 3) -> story 5
P17 a new test that fails because the code does not exist yet counts as failing today (owner's answer 2) -> story 2

stories.title: Plan checker: kinds, sources and named tests
stories.user_story: Owners only see plans whose sources point at their issue and whose named tests are real and filed under the plan's own criteria.
stories.context: dokima/planner.py read_output still accepts question.md and a plan.json with no kind (the old objective/criteria shape); from_kind only checks a source is non-empty; declared_labels ignores named tests that do not exist, and counts only added or changed tests as proof, so a criterion named against an older unchanged test is rejected as 'has no test'. A number where text belongs crashes the check (c['text'][:60] in from_kind raises TypeError). Older tests in tests/test_planner.py that hand back question.md or the old shape will need changing, with reasons. The repo comes from GITHUB_REPOSITORY.

acceptance_criteria.text: A hand-back that is not a plan.json naming one of the kinds user_story, feature or question (a question.md, or a plan.json with no kind) is rejected, and the reason says plan.json must name one of the three kinds.

A criterion whose source is anything other than this issue's link or a link to one of its comments (#issuecomment-...) is rejected, and the reason names the source; this issue's link and its comment links pass.

A test the plan names that is not in the repo, or that is filed under a key that is not one of this plan's criteria (another issue's number, or past the last criterion), is rejected, and the reason names the test or the key.
A criterion proven only by an older test that is already in the repo counts as proven, not as 'has no test'.

non_functional.text: A plan.json with a value of the wrong type (a number where text belongs, a string where a list belongs) is rejected with a reason naming the field, never a crash.
non_functional.why: a crash posts nothing and leaves the owner guessing

stories.title: Plan checker: new tests are checked as new, renames as changes
stories.user_story: Every new test in a plan has a one-sentence summary and fails today, and renaming an older test is treated as a change with a reason.
stories.context: dokima/planner.py test_changes sees a rename as one deleted plus one added test (the false rejection on #138). Nothing reads docstrings or runs the new tests today. A rename is decided by code, not guessed from labels: a test whose source is unchanged apart from its name is a rename. The planner only writes tests, so the working tree is today's code. Builds on story 1's handling of named tests. The owner confirmed (answer 2 on the issue) that a new test which fails because the code it needs does not exist yet counts as failing today. Changed and deleted older tests already need a reason (dokima/planner.py problems, the 'older' list); that check stays as it is.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test with no docstring, or whose docstring's first line is not one plain sentence on one line (one sentence, ending in '.', '?' or '!'), is rejected, and the reason names the test.

Every new test is run on today's code; one that passes or is skipped is rejected, and the reason names the test and says it passes today. A test that fails, including one that errors because the feature it needs does not exist yet, passes the check.

A renamed older test (same source, new name) counts as a change: it needs a reason in test_changes under its old name, and it is not held to the docstring or must-fail rules for new tests; a rename with no reason is rejected, naming the old test.

non_functional.text: A new test file the checker cannot parse is rejected with a reason naming the file, never a crash.
non_functional.why: a crash posts nothing on the issue

non_functional.text: A new test still running after 60 s is stopped and rejected, naming the test.
non_functional.why: one hanging test must not hang the planner's run until it times out with no reason

stories.title: Plan checker: features and questions are checked
stories.user_story: A proposed split or a question reaches the owner only when it is complete: every story is well formed with sound dependencies, and every question has options and a recommendation.
stories.context: dokima/planner.py from_kind checks only that a feature has 2 to 5 stories, and that a question ends in '?'; options and recommendation are optional today. A feature whose story depends on itself, with an empty title, is accepted today. In a feature, criteria have no N.k numbers yet; code names story s's criterion k as 'S<s>.<k>' (for example S2.3), which story 4 and story 5 use when a review names a criterion of a split.

acceptance_criteria.text: A feature story missing its title, user_story, acceptance_criteria or a depends_on list is rejected, and the reason names the story and the field.
A story that depends on itself, on a story the feature does not have, or on others in a loop is rejected, and the reason names the story; a valid chain of dependencies passes.
A question with no options or no recommendation is rejected, and the reason says which is missing; a question with both passes.

stories.title: The worker's and reviewer's hand-backs are checked, and a rejection says why on the issue
stories.user_story: The worker's and the reviewer's hand-backs reach the owner only in the shape their prompts define, every blocker is about one of the plan's criteria, and a rejected run says why on the issue.
stories.context: dokima/agent.py problems_review and problems_work check a few fields, crash on a string where an object belongs (blockers: ['B1'] raises AttributeError) or a number where a list belongs (notes: 5 raises TypeError), never check work.json gives a line for every plan criterion, and only check that a blocker's criterion is non-empty. `agent check` does not get the plan or the issue number today, so .github/workflows/agent.yml must pass them; agent.yml also only writes a record on rejection and posts nothing on the issue (planner.yml does, through `planner rejected`). The prompts' shapes are in dokima/roles/reviewer.md and dokima/roles/worker.md (work.json says empty lists may be left out). The real files from #142 are not in the repo (no branch holds them); they live in GitHub run artifacts. The owner answered (answer 3) that every blocker names a criterion, with no exception; dropped asks are caught by story 5 instead. A plan-stage review of a split names a story's criterion as S<s>.<k> (story 3). The real hand-backs as test samples are story 5, once the format is settled.

acceptance_criteria.text: A review.json or work.json missing a required field of its prompt's shape, or holding a field of the wrong type or an item of the wrong shape (a note without text, a reply without why), is rejected, and the reason names the field; it never crashes.
A work.json that gives no line for a criterion of the approved plan, or a line for a criterion the plan does not have, is rejected, and the reason names the criterion.

A reviewer's blocker that names no criterion, or a criterion the plan does not have (N.k for a story, S<s>.<k> for a story of a split), or whose test is neither empty (a promise with no proof) nor one of the plan's tests for that criterion (a proof that proves nothing), is rejected, and the reason names the blocker.
When a worker's or reviewer's hand-back is rejected, the issue gets one comment listing every reason, with a link to the run.

stories.title: The reviewer lists every ask in the owner's words, and real hand-backs become test samples
stories.user_story: A plan never drops one of the owner's asks unnoticed: the reviewer reads the issue on its own and lists every ask it finds, each matched to a criterion or marked missing.
stories.context: The owner's answer 3 on the issue: the planner cannot check itself for dropped asks because it writes the criteria from the owner's words, so the reviewer reads the issue text on its own and lists every ask; review.json gets a field for exactly this, and the checker rejects a plan review without it. The review.json shape lives in dokima/roles/reviewer.md (the owner asks for this change, so editing dokima/roles/ is allowed here) and is checked by dokima/agent.py problems_review. Proposed shape: "asks": [{"ask": "the owner's words", "source": "issue or comment link", "criterion": "N.k" | "S<s>.<k>" | "missing"}]. A plan that is a question has no criteria, so its review may give an empty asks list. Answer 1: keep real JSON hand-backs from this run as test samples once the format is settled; the records in .dokima/139/ written before this story (01-planner.json, 02-reviewer-plan.json) predate the asks field, so the samples are hand-backs recorded after stories 1 to 4 land, copied into tests/samples/.

acceptance_criteria.text: The reviewer's prompt tells it to read the owner's issue text and comments on its own and hand back, in review.json, an asks list: every ask it finds, in the owner's words with a link to where they said it, each matched to one of the plan's criteria or marked missing.

A plan review of a story or a split with no asks list, an empty one, or an ask missing its words, its link or its match is rejected, and the reason names what is missing; an ask matched to a criterion the plan does not have is rejected, naming the ask.
A plan review that marks any ask missing cannot approve: an approve with a missing ask is rejected, and the reason names the ask.
Real plan.json, review.json and work.json hand-backs recorded from this issue's run after the format is settled are kept under tests/samples/, and each passes its checker on every test run.

questions: When the reviewer marks one of your asks missing, should that alone stop the plan, or only be listed for you? I planned for: a plan review with a missing ask cannot approve (story 5), so a dropped ask always sends the plan back to the planner.

concerns.text: Half the original list is already built and tested since this issue was written: kinds and required fields, a reason on every non-functional requirement, tests-folder-only, 2 to 5 stories, a question ending in '?'. The split covers only what is still missing.
